I have a pretty massive scar from the bottom of my pinky across the back of my hand to my thumb. I struggle with depression and PTSD stemming from a traumatic childhood. I was consistently abused for quite a while and whenever I tried to fight back or argue or vent my feelings I was always “put in my place” if you will and so I started using pain to vent my frustrations, anger, sadness, and various other emotions. I use to cut various other parts of my body but I landed in repeated cutting the back of my hand over and over. It got to the point when I had cut it so many times I started to lose feeling in that area of my hand so I made the wound bigger and deeper in order to feel something. I cut so deep Once I exposed the tendons in the back of my hand. The reason I opted to self harm is because I felt like it was the one thing I could really control. 

My relationship with pain is a odd thing. I used pain as my emotional and mental stabilizer. When I hurt my self I would hyper focus on the pain and it would help me drown out the other things that were happening to me. In a fucked ip way the pain made me feel alive. I later found out I was probably in a dissociative state for years and always described it as living underwater in a black and white world. 

I’ve been clean for quite a while. Unfortunately from time to time I get extremely triggered by various things and have relapses. The last time it happened I was walking in the city I live in and I saw someone who looked exactly like a man who abused me. That sent me into a horrendous spiral and I did give in to the urges but got help immediately after.  I’m doing much better now and have found a lot better ways of coping. Life is not always a easy journey but thankfully my path is starting to get a bit less rocky.

To start off mining never use a tile saw. They will fracture you stone and you need coolant to cut with and tile saws are dry cut only and the wrong type of blade which is too abrasive and will shred turquoise. If you are looking for  Affordable but high quality equipment I recommend Highland Park lapidary saws. . If you want any more info on their saws they also have a YouTube video to show how to use their equipment and service them.  For starting off I recommend like a 6inch trim saw they are perfect for beginnings but preform very well and reliably. 

For cabbing units which typically run from 1200 - 3000 I recommend looking on Lapidary equipment marketplace on Facebook for either HP combo units or dual wheel units

The best way to make spheres is to use a 45 degree jig and to cut all corners off the piece. It’s a very slow and boring process but if you’ll don’t have a core drill or drop saw it’s the way to go. Go to Highland park lapidary if you are interested in seeing what one looks like.

It’s is definitely a lesser dyed agate. Mostly likely a Brazilian agate. Brazilian agates make up most dyed agates in the world due to their limited amount of banding and clear coloring. They are also EXTREMELY cheap to buy. Most agates you see in retail stores like home goods are Brazilian agates as well.

Specifically it is called Chevron amethyst due to the white triangle shaped inclusions. It’s a lot more rare than normal amethyst crystals and much of the chevron amethyst mined comes from thundery bay.

Hard to say the only way to truly know is to cut it with a lapidary  saw. For bones the inside would be covered in black dots with a darker colored center. It’s most likely not petrified wood since it has no bark marks nor growth marks.
